claim.purpose: Resolve #5664 protocol-adapter mTLS and Runtime control body-bound closeout blockers

initial.title: [v0.91.8][runtime-v3][protocols] Resolve #5664 terminal closeout security blockers
initial.goal: Fix the two accepted #5664 terminal-closeout security blockers so #5664 can be closed out truthfully.
initial.required_outcome: Runtime v3 protocol adapters have a current authenticated TLS client-identity boundary or equivalent, Runtime control rejects oversized inbound bodies at the route boundary, and focused tests prove both negative paths.
initial.task_boundary: Bounded Runtime v3 security repair for #5755 only; no AWS and no broad Runtime v3 implementation.
initial.plan_summary: Add the smallest protocol-adapter client-auth/equivalent boundary and explicit Runtime control body limit, then validate with focused protocol/control tests and exact-head review.
dependencies: #5664 terminal closeout remains blocked until this issue is fixed or re-dispositioned
deliverables: Protocol adapter authenticated TLS client identity or explicit equivalent security boundary
Runtime control explicit request body bound
Focused negative tests for missing client identity/equivalent and oversized control input
Exact-head review and truthful C-SDLC records
acceptance_criteria: Networked protocol adapter security no longer relies on no-client-auth TLS for the production boundary.
Runtime control route rejects oversized request bodies before unbounded JSON parsing.
Focused tests cover the fixed security boundaries and fail-closed negative cases.
No AWS work or credential exposure.
PR body closes #5755 and references #5664 closeout unblock truth.
invariants: No plaintext credentials or credential material in tracked artifacts.
No terminal closeout for #5664 until exact-head review confirms these blockers are resolved.
Keep changes bounded to Runtime v3 protocol/control security.
authority_boundary: Issue #5664 terminal closeout consumes the result after merge.
No AWS or external infrastructure authority.
non_goals: Do not redesign Runtime v3 protocols.
Do not perform AWS provisioning or cloud experiments.
Do not close #5664 by ignoring accepted security defects.
operator_constraints: no tracked product edits on main
initial.failure_policy: Fail closed if either security blocker remains unproven or exact-head review is stale.
risks: mTLS changes can over-widen protocol API surface if not kept minimal.
Body-limit tests must prove the route boundary, not only helper parsing.

steps.action: Patch protocol adapter security boundary and tests.
Patch Runtime control body bound and oversized-body tests.
Run focused validation, exact-head review, publish and shepherd PR.

validation_lanes.proof_role: Prove protocol adapter authenticated TLS/equivalent negative and positive paths.
Prove oversized Runtime control requests are rejected at the route boundary.
Prove textual diff hygiene for Runtime v3 security repair.
Record exact-head review for #5755 before publication and #5664 closeout consumption.

initial.review_scope: Exact-head review of protocol adapter security, Runtime control body-bound behavior, and focused tests.
review_prompts: Does the protocol adapter security repair close the accepted #5664 mTLS/client-auth or equivalent boundary without overclaiming?
Does the Runtime control route reject oversized request bodies before unbounded JSON parsing?
Are tests focused and sufficient for the two accepted blockers?
stop_conditions: Stop if the repair requires AWS or external infrastructure.
Stop if typed lifecycle cannot bind #5755 without hand editing generated state.
Stop if exact-head review finds an unresolved P1/P2 security blocker.
